name: らぁ麺や ふぢとら (Raamenya Fujitora)

claims.text: House-made wheat noodles are milled and cut fresh in the shop every morning, so wheat flour handling is central to the kitchen and cross-contact is unavoidable.
The shoyu tare blends six soy sauces (based on Kaneiwa of Wakayama and Suehiro of Hyogo) — standard wheat-fermented Japanese shoyu — so the soy ramen is wheat-based at its core.

Broth is made from jidori chicken bones, kurobuta pork and pork back bone and finished with chicken oil; toppings include pork chashu, ground pork and meat-filled wontons, so no bowl is free of animal products.

name: ラーメン あかつき (Ramen Akatsuki)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water, and the broth is finished with a soy-sauce tare that is essentially always wheat-based — pervasive gluten with no separation.
The bowl is a shoyu (soy sauce) ramen finished with a Japanese-dashi soy tare; standard Japanese shoyu is brewed with wheat.
The base soup is a pork-bone and chicken broth with back-fat and braised pork char siu; there is no animal-free preparation, so all bowls carry animal product.

All ramen, including the vegan bowls, uses wheat noodles; the seasoning is wheat-based shiro-tamari or soy sauce. No gluten-free noodle or tare exists here, so the kitchen has no gluten-free workflow.
Tare is naturally-fermented shiro-tamari (a white tamari/soy) or soy sauce, both wheat-containing.

The vegan ramen (vegetable salt, vegetable 'tonkotsu-style', and 100% vegan Shinshu-miso) is genuinely plant-based by recipe, but it is cooked in the same small kitchen as chicken-clear, chicken-paitan and spiny-lobster broths with pork chashu, so shared pots/utensils are likely.
Multiple dedicated vegan bowls are a permanent menu item, and the kitchen emphasizes additive-free ingredients, which is reassuring for plant-based diners by ingredient.

name: ラーメン池田屋 京都一乗寺店 (Ramen Ikedaya Kyoto Ichijoji-ten)

claims.text: Core dish is thick wheat ramen noodles made with Nisshin Seifun wheat flour, served from a small single-counter kitchen with shared boiling water, making gluten cross-contamination effectively unavoidable.
The broth is finished with a soy-based (shoyu) tare, which in standard ramen contains wheat; no wheat-free tare is mentioned.
Broth is an emulsified pork-bone/pork-fat base with pork back-fat and pork chashu; vegetables are cooked within this pork-based system, so no vegan-safe preparation exists.

name: ラーメン二郎 京都店 (Ramen Jiro Kyoto-ten)

claims.text: All bowls use wheat noodles boiled in a shared pot with a wheat-based soy tare; there is no gluten-free preparation or separation, so cross-contamination is unavoidable.
The tare is a soy-sauce base typical of Jiro-style ramen, which uses wheat-containing soy sauce; soy sauce is also offered as a counter condiment.
The broth is a pork and back-fat stock and bowls include chashu pork; even the vegetable topping (boiled bean sprouts and cabbage) is served in pork broth, so no item is free of animal products.
The tare is made from honjozo (conventionally brewed, wheat-containing) soy sauce combined with kombu, fish stock and white dashi, so the shoyu base contains wheat.
The Kyoto dashi broth is built on kombu plus fish/seafood stock and white dashi, and bowls carry pork chashu and fried beef intestine, so the kitchen handles animal products throughout.

name: ラーメン まきさだ (Ramen Makisada)

claims.text: 看板のまきさだラーメンは醤油ラーメンで、醤油（しょうゆ）ベースのタレを用いる。通常のしょうゆは小麦を含むため、グルテン回避者には不向き。
スープは動物系の出汁で、トッピングは細切りチャーシュー（豚）、サイドの焼売も豚肉。植物性のみの選択肢は確認できない。

name: らーめん門扇 伏水酒蔵店 (Ramen Monsen Fushimi Sakagura-ten)

claims.text: No source documents the tare composition, but a chicken-broth ramen of this style is conventionally seasoned with wheat-based shoyu; not confirmed gluten-free.
The broth is a chicken-bone (tori-gara/tori-paitan) stock simmered with vegetables, so no bowl is free of animal product even before toppings.
